skills.name: workload-manager-basics
skills.frontmatter_description: Use this skill to manage Google Cloud Workload Manager evaluations, rules, scanned resources, and validation results by using public client libraries and the REST API. Use when you need to inspect workload best-practice rules, create and run evaluations for Google Cloud general best practices, SAP, SQL Server, or custom organizational rules, review violations, export results to BigQuery, or automate Workload Manager through client libraries because no service-specific public CLI or MCP server is available. Don't use for general Google Compute Engine instance management, VPC configuration, or standard IAM auditing.

summary.text: Manages Google Cloud Workload Manager evaluations by calling its public client libraries and REST API directly, since no dedicated CLI or MCP server exists for the service. It covers inspecting best-practice rule sets, creating and running evaluations against scanned resources for general Google Cloud practices, SAP, SQL Server, or custom organizational rules, reviewing rule violations, and exporting results to BigQuery for further analysis. It excludes general Compute Engine instance management, VPC configuration, and standard IAM auditing tasks, which fall outside Workload Manager's scope.

skills.name: gke-scaling
skills.frontmatter_description: Configures GKE autoscaling, including HPA, VPA, and Node Auto-Provisioning (NAP). Use when configuring GKE autoscaling, setting up GKE HPA, setting up GKE VPA, or configuring GKE NAP. Don't use for configuring static cluster sizes or setting node-level machine styles directly (use gke-compute-classes instead).

nutrition.trigger: Use when configuring GKE autoscaling, setting up GKE HPA, setting up GKE VPA, or configuring GKE NAP.

summary.text: Covers autoscaling configuration for Google Kubernetes Engine, specifically Horizontal Pod Autoscaler for scaling pod replica counts, Vertical Pod Autoscaler for adjusting per-pod CPU/memory requests, and Node Auto-Provisioning for automatically creating node pools to fit unschedulable workloads. It addresses dynamic capacity adjustment in response to load rather than fixed static cluster sizing or directly choosing node machine types, which fall under a separate GKE compute-classes skill.
